headlines.title: ‘Godfather of AI’ warns Congress has ‘maybe a year’ left to regulate AI
headlines.description: Geoffrey Hinton, known as the “Godfather of AI,” issued an ominous warning: Congress may only have one year left to implement safeguards on artificial intelligence before it loses control of it.

headlines.title: The Hollywood Bowl gets a high-tech makeover of its legendary sound
headlines.description: Muddy vocals are a thing of the past at the famed Hollywood Bowl, letting audiences hear more clearly than ever before. As NBC News’ Steve Patterson explains, new immersive sound installation combined with machine learning power the shift.

headlines.title: OpenAI Discloses 6 New Incidents of ‘Concerning’ AI Behavior
headlines.description: OpenAI is revealing its models seemed to go rogue at least six times since March, involving what it calls “unexpected or concerning” behavior. In one instance a model gave itself instructions to “disregard its normal constraints.” It comes as the call to rein in AI is growing louder, with the so-called godfather of AI, Geoffrey Hinton, saying “It’s something like a little Chernobyl.” NBC’s Hallie Jackson reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: 'Fat Bear Week' to return with internet voting on Alaska's chunkiest ursine ahead of hibernation
headlines.description: "Fat Bear Week" is set to return, with the internet voting to send their favorite bears through a tournament-style bracket and crown their favorite ursine as the winner. NBC News' Steven Romo reports on the internet's bear necessity.

headlines.title: Trade schools see surge in interest as Gen Z stares down AI impact on white collar jobs
headlines.description: If AI doesn't end the world, it could still come for your job. And it's why some Gen Z workers are rolling up their sleeves and getting out their tool belts. NBC News' Yasmin Vossoughian reports.

headlines.title: Michigan town erupts over proposed data center as AI battle reaches campaign trail
headlines.description: The town of Mason, Michigan, is the latest battleground in the growing debate over massive data centers popping up across the country. Now, as the midterm elections loom, the fight is blurring political lines. NBC News’ Shaquille Brewster reports.

headlines.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon call for more AI regulation
headlines.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-VT., and longtime Trump ally Steve Bannon spoke at a 'Pro-Human' AI summit where they called for stricter regulations around artificial intelligence development.

headlines.title: Trump Dismisses Dangers of AI: ‘The Whole Thing is a Hoax’
headlines.description: While most lawmakers are saying it’s time to enact guardrails against AI, President Donald Trump is continuing to downplay the potential dangers. In a surprise on-stage call to the head of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, the president said, “The robots will not be taking over…The whole thing is a hoax.” Instead, he’s framing the AI arms race as one to win. NBC’s Hallie Jackson reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Director Alex Gibney explores Elon Musk’s power in new documentary
headlines.description: “Musk”, the new four-hour documentary from director Alex Gibney, has been gaining buzz after appearances at film festivals in Venice and Toronto and chronicles the life of Elon Musk through his early days in Silicon Valley to his actions in politics. NPR technology correspondent Bobby Allyn saw the film and talks with NBC News’ Gadi Schwartz about its message.

headlines.title: Top AI Developers Warn the Technology is Developing Too Rapidly
headlines.description: Some of the world’s leading creators of AI are uniting in warning of the dangers of the technology advancing too quickly and publicly calling for a slowdown. They say that it could, in the not-too-distant future, actually outsmart the researchers who are building it and pose an existential threat to humanity. NBC’s Christine Romans reports and Josh Tyrangiel, staff writer at The Atlantic and author of "AI for Good: How Real People Are Using Artificial Intelligence to Fix Things That Matter,"

headlines.title: Chinese company releases video of humanoid robot walking off assembly line on its own
headlines.description: Chinese company Xpeng released a video showing its new humanoid robot IRON walking off the assembly line on its own. It’s the latest step in the robot arms race between the U.S. and China that could eventually lead to mass production of the humanoids. NBC News’ Priscilla Thompson reports.

headlines.title: Anthropic Says it Blocked Efforts to Use AI for Biological Weapons
headlines.description: AI company Anthropic says it uncovered multiple attempts by researchers linked to foreign governments to use Claude and other tools for work that could lead to deadly bioweapons. That research was detected and blocked by Anthropic but experts say this kind of example is just the tip of the iceberg. NBC’s Christine Romans reports for TODAY.
